title: Keep read requests in the plan and drain queue
summary: Reading a request currently moves it from queued to proposed, so plan and drain drop it. Make read requests stay in the plan and the drain queue, and explain or fix why plan at the default budget 2 reads none. The audience is the maintainer running plan and drain.

defaults_applied.how: Regression tests plus cargo test and clippy.
Fix the queue-state handling, not just the plan output.
Criteria check that read requests stay in plan and drain.
Behavior is exercised by CLI tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: the maintainer running athena plan and drain on a real queue. Read requests must stay in plan and drain.
The fix is to make plan and drain treat read (proposed) requests as workable, or to keep them queued after reading. I chose this over a new state.
The default budget 2 reading none is a separate symptom. I will make it consistent, with a test, only if the cause is simple.
Exact files are not confirmed. They are guessed from grep hits on Proposed in steward.rs, drain.rs, main.rs, and reading.rs.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test queues several unread requests, runs plan with a budget that reads some, then checks the read requests still appear in the plan and in the drain's queue. Run `cargo test`.
After `athena plan --budget N` reads requests, `athena plan` does not say nothing is open, and drain still has the read requests to work. Checked by a stub-backed CLI test run with `cargo test`.
A request that has been read is still schedulable by plan and drain (it is no longer dropped from the queue). Its state or its selection is changed at the root cause, not only in plan.
The default budget gives the reading room to read unread requests, or the 'no room in the job limit or the budget' message is explained and covered by a test. Run `cargo test`.
`cargo test` passes, `cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
README/help and CHANGELOG describe that reading keeps requests queued. The misleading test name from the earlier verification is fixed.

out_of_scope: Making plan read-only by default (an earlier nit, not requested here).
Redesigning the job state machine beyond keeping read requests workable.
departures: The change spans state handling and plan/drain, so cost and time run somewhat above the reference.
